inferred that the collective function of the tissue was to form a thermogenic jacket, particularly during the ﬁrst years of life when
other heat regulation mechanisms have not yet matured sufﬁciently to protect against cold. It was assumed that BAT gradually dis-
appeared in later stages of life as the thermogenic capacity of the jacket was no longer required.
However, an investigation of cadaver tissue of winter outdoor workers in 1981 found evidence of greater BAT presence in adult
humans adapted to cold. BAT was found in the neck and the pericardium of outdoor workers, compared to indoor workers who had
none. The amount of BAT was greater in outdoor workers who were exposed to cold recently, as the outdoor worker who perished in
February had more multilocular adipose tissue than the worker who died in August. Similarly, retired farmers also showed a decrease
